data.narrative:
Oxford Quantum Circuits is a Series C-stage quantum computing company that has raised $350M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 comparable entities—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum and Infleqtion—though few provide direct valuation precedent at Oxford's stage and tier.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable method here. Using total capital raised of $350M as a baseline and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement yields an implied valuation of $595M. A peer-median approach was not feasible; while 6 same-sector comparables exist, none met the minimum threshold of three datapoints when filtered by stage, timing, or valuation tier, making a narrow peer set insufficient to ground a reliable median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $506M to $684M, centered on $595M. This range reflects approximately ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include the absence of validated private-market comparables at similar stage and valuation, limiting independent cross-check capability, and the inherent volatility of early-stage quantum computing valuations amid rapidly shifting technical feasibility claims and competitive positioning. Any refinement would require additional private-market transaction data or clearer articulation of Oxford's technical differentiation relative to the public-market cohort.
